newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU calls for release of Burmese detainees.
newsitem.headline: EU calls for release of Burmese detainees.

text.p: The European Union called on Tuesday for the immediate release of more than 500 people detained by Burmese military rulers in a crackdown on pro-democracy activists.

EU foreign ministers released a statement saying they were very concerned at the situation in Burma and calling on its ruling State Law and Order Restoration Committee (SLORC) to lift a blockade on the home of opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi.

Burma's military government said on Tuesday it had released 88 of the 559 supporters of the National League for Democracy (NLD) party held since Thursday but roadblocks around Suu Kyi's remained in place.
Senior Burmese officials said detained activists were being held temporarily to prevent unrest and would be released soon.

The EU foreign ministers said: "The European Union wishes to emphasise the need for a genuine dialogue to commence without delay between SLORC and the NDL as being the only possible credible way forward for national reconciliation."
